goal: A masters-level seminar deck on how cultural diversity and national identity in Bangladesh have been shaped historically and politically — verified facts only, 17 slides, 10–15 minute talk, with speaker notes.

deck_context.source_summary: Bangladesh: 169.8M people (Census 2022 final); Muslim 91.04%, Hindu 7.95%, Buddhist 0.61%, Christian 0.30%, other 0.12%. ~54 indigenous peoples, ≥35 languages (Census counts 1,650,159 across 50 groups; activist estimates ≥3M). ~1.1–1.2M Rohingya. CHT Accord 1997 unfinished. Constitutional arc: secularism 1972 → removed (Fifth Amendment) → state religion 1988 (Eighth) → restored + Article 12 (Fifteenth, 2011). 2024 uprising; 12 Feb 2026 election (BNP 209/297); Tarique Rahman PM from 17 Feb 2026; minority posture tested Oct 2026.
deck_context.core_claim: Bangladesh's national identity is a negotiated balance between the unifying forces of language and 1971 memory and the country's deep religious, ethnic, and cultural plurality — the terms of that balance are still being contested today.

slides.title: Constitution, Principles, and the Secularism Debate
slides.intent: Present the constitutional journey of secularism as the spine of the identity debate
key_points: 1972 — Four principles: nationalism, socialism, democracy, secularism
Fifth Amendment (1977/1979) — secularism removed; Bismillah inserted
Eighth Amendment 1988 — Islam, the state religion · 2005 High Court: removal of secularism illegal
Fifteenth Amendment 2011 — secularism restored; Article 12 anti-communalism; Article 2A keeps Islam as state religion
